newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rover to make new Mini.
newsitem.headline: Rover to make new Mini.

text.p: British carmaker Rover, owned by Germany's Bayerischen Motoren Werke BMW, will make a new mini at its Longbridge plant, the chairman of BMW said on Tuesday.

Bernd Pischetsrieder told a news conference during the Paris car show that the new mini would be powered by 1.4 and 1.6 four cylinder engines to be built at a new joint venture plant with Chrysler Corp in Latin America.
This plant will make 400,000 engines per year of which half will be for the BMW/Rover group and the other half for Chrysler, which will use them for the Neon car.
Pischetsrieder said the engine deal meant that "there is room for another existing mass production car at Longbridge, the new mini."
He also said that the new four-cylinder engines would replace Rover's A-series engines but not its K-series which will be replaced at a later stage with a joint Rover/BMW powerplant
The mini started as an Austin Morris made by British Leyland and it was, with Fiat's Cinquecento, among the first minicars in Europe that obtained a big and loyal following.

Following the launch of Renault's Twingo in the early 90s, minicars regained their appeal and many carmakers are launching vehicles in the sector. Ford Motor Co in Paris unveiled its Ka model which is its smallest offering.
